<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - FileCodeBox is a monolithic full-stack application for anonymous file/text sharing, built with FastAPI (backend) and Vue 3 (frontend).  
   - The backend serves both the REST API and the compiled Vue frontend assets (in `themes/2023` and `themes/2024`).  
   - Core features: upload/download via extraction codes, admin panel, pluggable storage (local, S3, OneDrive), rate limiting, expiration.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level:  
     • `main.py` – entrypoint to start FastAPI.  
     • `apps/` – application modules:  
       – `apps/base/` (upload/download business logic)  
       – `apps/admin/` (management UI APIs)  
     • `core/` – shared services: configuration, DB session, storage abstraction, logger, background tasks.  
     • `themes/` – compiled Vue 3 frontend for two UI themes; includes `index.html` and static assets.  
     • `docs/` – documentation site (VitePress) – not part of runtime.  
     • `docker-compose.yml` / `Dockerfile` – container definitions.  
   - Config: `requirements.txt`, `.env` loaded by `core/settings.py`.  
   - Data directories: at runtime a `data` volume for SQLite and uploaded files.

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Stack: FastAPI, SQLite (default), Vue3 + ElementUI.  
   - Features: extraction codes, expiration, admin dashboard, storage engines.  
   - Deployment: Docker CLI / Compose, or manual `python main.py`.  
   - Admin panel at `/#/admin`, protected by a password.

4. System design diagram: how to draw it  
   a. Main components  
      - Client layer  
        • Web browser (end-user UI)  
        • CLI (optional)  
      - API & Static Server  
        • FastAPI application  
        • Vue3 static frontend (served from `themes/…`)  
      - Business modules  
        • Base module (`apps/base`): upload/download, code generation  
        • Admin module (`apps/admin`): settings, file management  
      - Core services  
        • Database service (`core/database.py` executing SQLite or configurable RDBMS)  
        • Storage service (`core/storage.py` for local FS or remote S3/OneDrive)  
        • Background Tasks (`core/tasks.py` for cleanup, expiration)  
        • Logger, Settings (`core/logger.py`, `core/settings.py`)  
      - Data stores  
        • File volume (local or mounted)  
        • SQLite DB file (in data volume)  
      - External services (optional)  
        • S3-compatible storage  
        • OneDrive OAuth/API  

   b. Relationships & interactions  
      - Browser sends HTTP(S) requests to FastAPI endpoints (upload/download/admin).  
      - FastAPI routes requests to appropriate `apps/base` or `apps/admin` handlers.  
      - Handlers use `core/database` to read/write metadata (extraction codes, file records).  
      - For file content, handlers use `core/storage` to persist or retrieve actual bytes.  
      - `core/tasks` runs asynchronously (or via scheduler) to purge expired entries.  
      - Admin UI interacts over same API with elevated permissions.  

   c. Architectural patterns / design principles  
      - Modular separation: controllers (`views.py`), services (`services.py`), schemas, dependencies.  
      - Dependency injection (FastAPI’s Depends) for DB sessions, storage engines.  
      - Pluggable storage adapter pattern for multiple backends.  
      - Single-process monolith that can be containerized with Docker.  

   d. Key technologies  
      - FastAPI (ASGI server)  
      - Uvicorn/Gunicorn (where deployed)  
      - SQLite (default) or other SQL DB via SQLAlchemy  
      - Python background tasks (Celery or FastAPI’s built-in)  
      - Vue3 + ElementUI (static assets in `themes/`)  
      - Docker / Docker Compose  

5. Tailoring guidelines  
   - Emphasize frontend vs. backend separation: one box for the browser UI (static). Another for FastAPI REST server.  
   - Show how pluggable storage implements both local and cloud options.  
   - Highlight the admin panel as a sub-component of the API.  
   - Note Docker container boundary: mount points for data volume.  

6. Diagram elements to include  
   - Boxes with clear labels: “Browser UI (Vue3)”, “FastAPI App”, “Base Module”, “Admin Module”, “SQLite DB”, “File Storage”, “Background Tasks”.  
   - Directional arrows for request/response flows:  
     • Browser → FastAPI → DB / Storage → FastAPI → Browser  
     • Scheduler → DB → Storage (for cleanup)  
   - Use colors or shapes:  
     • Blue for user-facing components (UI & API)  
     • Green for data stores  
     • Orange for background tasks  
     • Gray dashed for optional external services  

7. Final tips  
   - Be thorough: include every sub-system (core settings, logger, storage).  
   - Don’t overthink: dozens of boxes are fine as long as they reflect each Python package or service.  
   - Show container boundary: Docker container hosting the FastAPI service and mounting the `data` volume.  

Use a tool like diagrams.net or Lucidchart; layer your diagram if it becomes too dense: separate “runtime components” from “external integrations.”  
Ensure the diagram captures all major modules (`apps/base`, `apps/admin`, `core/...`), data flows, and storage backends.  
</explanation>
